figures.finding: The national government levies a wage and salary tax (with a tax-free threshold) and a gross receipts tax on business, half of each shared with the states; their rates were not found.

sources.said: the State Governments will maintain its eighty percent (80%)of the fuel tax collected and its original fifty percent (50%)of the wage and salary tax, gross receipts tax, and import duties other than the fuel tax.
the proposed transition from the Gross Revenue Tax to a Net Profits Tax. The introduction of a Value Added Tax and a proposed increase to the wage and salary tax threshold were also discussed.

figures.finding: There is no VAT in force: its introduction was still under discussion by the national tax reform task force in November 2025.

sources.said: The introduction of a Value Added Tax and a proposed increase to the wage and salary tax threshold were also discussed.

figures.finding: Social Security tax is 7.5% of taxable wages from the worker and 7.5% from the employer (15% combined), on wages up to $7,000 a quarter; a self-employed person with no employees and over $10,000 of gross revenue reports quarterly wages for himself of 5% of the year's gross revenue and pays the 15% on them (with employees, twice the highest-paid employee's wages).
figures.applies: From 1 January 2013 (the statutory rise from 7% to 7.5% each); the quarterly base as FSMSSA states it ("currently").

sources.said: The statutory SS tax rate increase would increase the employee’s share of contributions from 7% to 7.5% of taxable wages and would also increase the employer’s matching contribution by the same rate, for a total of 2% increase in the combined SS tax rate (15%).
Currently the maximum quarterly taxable wage base is $7,000.
If gross revenues exceed $10,000, then these self-employed persons must report gross wages for themselves for each calendar quarter equal to 5% of the business’ gross revenues for the calendar year.
Quarterly Social Security Tax Due = $800 x 15% = $120.00
Self-employed persons with employees must report gross wages for themselves equal to twice the wages of the highest paid employee reported by them for that quarter.

figures.finding: The employer deducts the Wage & Salaries Tax from an employee's pay and remits it to the Customs and Tax Administration; a contractor who is in business (controls the work, risks own money) registers instead for the Gross Revenue Tax and files its returns.
figures.applies: FSM national taxes; the rates (Title 54) are not read, see the residents blocker.

sources.said: The contractor permits the Department or Agency (employer) to deduct the Wage & Salaries Tax (W&ST) from their payments for services from the commencement of this contract, and pay the amounts deducted to the Customs and Tax Administration (CTA) to be credited against the W&ST payable by the contractor.
